requirement:
`habeas status` MUST group the selected requirement and example judgments marked
FIXME by issue reference and report how many distinct judgments each issue
affects. It MUST recognize `#123` and `owner/repo#123` within recorded FIXME
strings, including `FIXME(...)` and explanatory text. A GitHub issue URL such as
`https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123` MUST identify the same issue as
`owner/repo#123`. Issue numbers MUST be positive, complete numeric tokens with
leading zeros normalized; repository spelling MUST remain case-sensitive, and
unqualified and qualified references MUST remain distinct.

A judgment MUST count at most once for each issue, even when that issue occurs
repeatedly or in several FIXME strings. A judgment naming several issues MUST
count in each corresponding group. Judgments with no recognized issue in any
FIXME string MUST be counted once in a separate "FIXME without an issue" group.
Issue groups MUST be ordered by decreasing affected-judgment count, then by
normalized reference; the group without an issue MUST follow them. A supplied
selection MUST restrict these counts to the selected subjects.

`--verbose` MUST list the full name and kind of every judgment in each issue
group and in the group without an issue, along with its original FIXME strings.
The summary MUST include valid FIXME determinations even when other evidence
checks fail; grouping MUST NOT hide their validation findings. Malformed
determinations MUST remain validation errors under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.
rationale:
## Judgment

The summary logic itself looks correct and well tested. The one gap is that some code which carries part of the requirement is not marked `{impl}` for it.

### Implementation, as marked
- **Plumbing.** `src/main.rs` `Status { all, selection, verbose }` calls `status_markdown_with_options`. That function in `src/commands.rs` skips terms, applies the glob, and calls `fixmes.add(...)` only for selected definitions, so counts are restricted to the selection. All of these are marked `{impl}`.
- **Issue recognition.** `issue_references` in `src/fixme.rs` finds `#N` and `owner/repo#N`. It also finds `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/N`, normalized to `owner/repo#N`.
  - It strips leading zeros and rejects `#0` and `#000`.
  - It rejects incomplete tokens such as `#12abc` and `##123`.
  - It keeps repository spelling case-sensitive and keeps unqualified and qualified references distinct.
  - It returns a `BTreeSet` per judgment, so a judgment counts at most once per issue, even across several strings.
- **Grouping and ordering.** `render` puts a judgment in every group it names. Judgments with no issue go in a single "FIXME without an issue" group after the issue groups. Groups sort by descending count, then by the normalized reference string.
  - The ordering is lexicographic, so `#123` sorts before `#45`. This is a defensible reading of "normalized reference", and the tests pin it.
- **Verbose output.** `--verbose` lists each judgment's full name, kind, and original FIXME strings (HTML-escaped) under every group and under the no-issue group.

### Gap: marking is incomplete
- The obligation "the summary MUST include valid FIXME determinations even when other evidence checks fail" is implemented in `LoadedDetailEvidence::load` in `src/index.rs`.
  - `load` parses `determination` and extracts `fixme_entries` independently of the `errors` list.
  - A malformed determination yields no entries, so it stays an Invalid validation error.
- The `load` function is marked only `requirements.index.state` and `requirements.ci.outcomes`.
- The accessors `LoadedDetailEvidence::fixme_entries` and `Judgment::fixme_entries` (`src/judgment.rs`) feed the summary. They are marked only `requirements.cli.status` and `requirements.index.detail_format`.
- None of these are marked `{impl}` for `requirements.cli.fixme_summary`. The `status` requirement text only says it summarizes "under" `fixme_summary`. It does not carry out the "even when other checks fail" and "malformed remains an error" obligations, and neither does `index.state`.
- The `--verbose` flag definition on `Command::Status` in `src/main.rs` is covered only by the `clap` marker (and `main` carries the fixme_summary marker). This is minor.
- These are partial implementations of the subject without an `{impl}` reference, which the review criteria treat as a gap.
- No FIXME comment or test acknowledges this gap, so the determination is `false`, not `FIXME`.

### Tests
Tests are strong:
- **`tests/commands.rs`: `status_groups_fixme_judgments_by_distinct_normalized_issue`.** It covers these cases:
  - zero normalization (`#00123`, `#000456`);
  - URL equivalence;
  - case-sensitive `Rust-Lang/rust` versus `rust-lang/rust`;
  - repeated references and multiple issues per judgment;
  - ordering by count and then reference;
  - the no-issue group coming last;
  - `#000`, `#12abc`, and `##123` not being recognized;
  - `--all` still showing the summary.
- **`tests/commands.rs`: `verbose_status_lists_fixme_judgments_and_globs_scope_issue_groups`.** It covers verbose listing, HTML escaping, and selection scoping.
- **Unit tests in `src/fixme.rs`.**
  - The URL-only test is `a_github_issue_url_alone_identifies_the_qualified_issue`.
  - The verbose multi-group test is `verbose_output_lists_each_judgment_under_every_group_it_belongs_to`.
- **`tests/outcomes.rs`.** These tests cover the interaction with other checks:
  - A malformed `FIXME: []` stays Invalid and produces no summary (`malformed_fixme_is_invalid_and_reports_the_required_shape`).
  - A stale input still shows both the `#125` group and the findings (`fixme_does_not_hide_stale_inputs_or_uncovered_references`).
  - A valid FIXME stays visible (`valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book`).

Test coverage is adequate. The sole blocker is the incomplete `{impl}` marking of the code that makes FIXME entries available regardless of other evidence failures. Adding `{impl}` markers for `requirements.cli.fixme_summary` there (and on the `--verbose` option) would resolve it.

Issue groups MUST be ordered by decreasing affected-judgment count, then by

:::{req} outcomes
A requirement or example judgment MUST use one of these outcomes, applying
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`:
- `true`: the sources support the subject and its testing obligations.
- `false`: the sources do not support the subject, or information is missing,
and the gaps are not all explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests.
- `FIXME`: some aspects remain unmet or untested, and source comments or tests
explicitly acknowledge those gaps. The reviewer MUST explain the gaps and
their source locations in the rationale and record their issue references or
other identifying content from the inputs.
The JSON `determination` MUST be `true`, `false`, or an object containing exactly
`"FIXME"` with a nonempty array of nonempty strings, such as
`{"FIXME": ["#125", "rust-lang/rust#123"]}`. The expected source convention is
`FIXME(issue-number)`, for example `FIXME(#125)` or
`FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123)`. References MAY appear elsewhere in the comment or
test; the reviewer MUST recognize explicit acknowledgments without requiring
that spelling. When no issue reference is present, the strings MUST identify the
documented gap using its source content. A FIXME judgment MUST be grounded in
recorded evidence inputs; a bare issue reference without an acknowledged gap
MUST NOT suffice.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
:::{definition} validation_error
:phrase: validation error
One message in a repository validation report, describing a single failed check.
It begins with the affected evidence file, requirement, or source location, names
the failed check, and states the specific missing, invalid, or changed value,
with the expected value when available. It is concise because agents are its
primary readers.
